competition.flat_book_pnl: A flat seat has zero net financing/competition P&L: paper NAV earning SOFR is benchmarked at SOFR, so those flows cancel, and shocked-risk financing is zero.
competition.funding_basis: Official NY Fed SOFR ACT/360 is the zero-return competition benchmark, not free alpha. Every seat has $100m paper NAV that may be described as earning SOFR, but that capital is equally funded/benchmarked at SOFR so those flows cancel. Deployed shocked-risk capital pays the same official SOFR on trusted standard-shock risk capital: the absolute MTM loss from a 1% adverse spot move, a 100bp (1 percentage point) adverse outright rate move, or a 100bp adverse curve/RV spread move. Supported STIR contracts use exchange DV01 and currency conversion; historical rows without that stamp keep the legacy duration-one vintage and are not silently restated. Equal risk capital receives equal financing treatment across asset classes. Notional is descriptive, not the funding base. A completely flat book — including no-trade-skeptic — therefore has zero net financing/competition P&L from SOFR cash or funding economics. Positive financing/carry alpha requires an explicit markable strategy that earns above SOFR or funds below SOFR. Weekends and holidays carry the last applicable published fixing until the next fixing. If official fixing history cannot be established, new funding accrual fails closed and prior canonical balances are preserved.
competition.instruction: Do not optimize for gross notional or fill available capacity. Size risk from plausible adverse paths and historical excursions while staying inside the trusted risk-capital and drawdown limits. Flat cash at SOFR is the zero benchmark, not a source of alpha. The no-trade-skeptic must include a structured funding_view on every new risk or NO_TRADE thesis: the frozen official SOFR fixing, the relevant SR3 forward-curve view, its own assessment of whether realized funding will print higher, lower, or about the same as the curve, and the implication for remaining at the zero SOFR benchmark versus paying SOFR on shocked-risk capital.
competition.objective: Finish with the highest cumulative net paper P&L across the 14 standing seats.

research_supplement.summary: The dollar is firm and stretched, core yields are high, and equities are still holding up while oil sits well below the triple-digit levels in older books. On the latest fixings WTI is 88.56 and Brent is 95.84, gold is 3886, and the S&P is 7562 with the VIX at 18.7. Euro-dollar at 1.1052 and the kiwi at 0.5532 are at multi-year lows, and dollar-yen is at 160. The US two-year is 4.88 and the ten-year is 5.15. Official SOFR is 3.90, while futures price a higher path, near 4.31 by December and about 4.60 by March 2027. Monday commentary talks about softer Treasuries ahead of Chair Warsh, but the last verified yield fixing is still Friday's backup. Ukraine's strike on the Crimean Bridge keeps a geopolitical bid in the energy story without lifting Brent back to those older levels. Canada inflation arrives after this cutoff, then Australian wages and euro-area prices midweek, with the Fed, the Bank of Canada, and the Reserve Bank of New Zealand on 9 December.

perma-bull.thesis: Hold the pro-growth pays at current size: short March 2027 SOFR in 50 million and short March 2027 AONIA in 35 million. Friday's verified fixings are a 4.88 percent US two-year and a 5.15 percent ten-year, SOFR futures still price hikes from 3.90 percent cash to about 4.60 in March 2027, and the S&P at 7562 with the VIX at 18.7 says expansion is absorbing that path. Brent at 95.84 and WTI at 88.56 are well below the old oil scare, so the oil kicker is weaker and size stays unchanged.
perma-bull.invalidation: The pays are wrong if March 2027 SOFR implied yield falls back through the 4.52 entry, or March 2027 AONIA through about 4.80, and Friday's 4.88 percent two-year and 5.15 percent ten-year fixings break lower.

actions.note: Hold the 50 million short March 2027 SOFR. The hike path is intact and weaker oil is not a reason to add.

rates_candidate.rationale: March 2027 SOFR near 4.60 still prices hikes above 3.90 percent cash, in line with the 4.88 percent two-year.

spot_candidate.rationale: Dollar-yen at 160 is the spot version of the same hike path and is already extended.

expression_memo.rationale: The SOFR pay is the pro-growth rates leg. Long dollar-yen at 160 is the spot twin, but it is already a five-year extreme, so the existing pay is the cleaner hold.

actions.note: Hold the 35 million short March 2027 AONIA. Cash near 4.85 and the March bill near 5.00 are a shallow hump, not a reason to add.

rates_candidate.rationale: March 2027 AONIA near 5.00 is only a little above cash near 4.85, and the position is already ahead of the 4.80 entry.

spot_candidate.rationale: Long Australian dollar at 0.6785 is the spot twin and fights the broad dollar.

expression_memo.rationale: The Australia pay is the same pro-growth hold. Long Australian dollar spot would fight a dollar that is already broad.

postmortems.thesis_assessment: The Canada pay was a pro-growth hike expression that needed a sustained oil impulse, and that impulse did not hold.
postmortems.what_failed: Oil cooled from the old scare to WTI 88.56 and Brent 95.84, and the short March 2027 Canada bill was closed while the curve still priced hikes.
postmortems.lesson: Do not treat a commodity-central-bank pay as the growth expression once oil has left the scare zone and the hike is already in the US strip.
postmortems.future_rule: Do not reopen or add a Canada pay while Brent is around 96 and WTI around 89. Keep the US SOFR pay that Friday's fixings still support, and do not treat a stronger score as permission to add.

causal.original_belief: A resilient growth tape plus oil in a scare zone would keep the Bank of Canada repricing the March 2027 bill higher from cash near 2.30 percent.
causal.observed_reality: The short was closed after oil had fallen to WTI 88.56 and Brent 95.84, while March Canada bills were still near 3.03 against cash near 2.30.
causal.assumptions_right: Risk appetite stayed expansionary, with the S&P at 7562 and the VIX at 18.7, and the US hike complex is still confirmed by Friday's higher yields.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: Oil was treated as persistent enough to carry a Canadian pay. The drop out of the scare zone, and Canada's oil beta, were underweighted.
causal.causal_divergence: The position lost money because the commodity catalyst faded inside a hike path that was already largely priced, while global growth did not collapse.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: With oil already off the scare and Canada inflation not yet in the evidence, the same information said to leave the Canada pay closed and keep the US SOFR pay.
causal.future_implication: Do not reopen the Canada pay and do not add the Australia or US pays just because the US growth tape is intact.

performance_reflections.what_happened_vs_expected: A rank swing that dwarfed a half-basis-point economic tick looked like a thesis break, and the later rank recovery looked like permission to add. The economic move was tiny, so the scoreboard gap was competition variance inside the risk budget.
performance_reflections.no_new_lesson: The original process remains sound. The rank swing was bounded variance inside the risk budget, and a recovered rank is not permission to add.

causal.original_belief: A rank drop much larger than the economic tick meant the pro-growth thesis had broken, and a later rank recovery would be permission to add.
causal.observed_reality: The economic move was only about half a basis point. The scoreboard gap came and went without a change in the hike path or the oil marks.
causal.assumptions_right: The live pays were still the growth expression, and the small tick did not change Friday's higher US yields or the SOFR strip.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: The rank gap was treated as information about the economy. It was a competition scoreboard move, and that distinction was underweighted in the moment.
causal.causal_divergence: Nothing in the rates path diverged. The only divergence was between a tiny mark and a large rank swing.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: With the same half-basis-point tick, the book would still be held at the same size and would not be increased after the rank recovered.
causal.future_implication: Do not add because a rank recovered, and do not cut because a rank fell, unless the yield path itself has changed.

perma-bear.thesis: Hold the US ten-year receive. The yield is 5.15, still short of the area near 5.24 where the long end had already been sold, and that duration is still the defensive expression. SOFR cash is 3.90 while futures price about 4.60 by March 2027, and the S&P at 7562 with the VIX at 18.7 has not marked the growth damage in that path. Oil at 88.56 and 95.84 did not confirm a shock, so selling an already-extended euro or kiwi would chase the dollar rather than hedge it.
perma-bear.invalidation: Cover the ten-year receive if the yield trades back through 5.24 while the S&P holds near 7562 and the VIX stays near 18.7, because that would validate the hike path in duration without a growth break.

actions.note: Hold the ten-year receive. The yield is 5.15 and equities have not marked the hike path.

rates_candidate.rationale: The ten-year at 5.15 is the defensive duration already held, still below the prior 5.24 area.

spot_candidate.rationale: The kiwi at 0.5532 is a high-beta risk-off spot, and it is already at multi-year lows.

expression_memo.rationale: The ten-year receive is the duration hedge. Selling the kiwi at 0.5532 or the euro at 1.1052 would chase a dollar that is already extended.

dollar-king.thesis: Cut the dollar-yen long from 20 million to 8 million and hold the 10 million euro-dollar short. Friday's two-year at 4.88 and ten-year at 5.15, with SOFR cash at 3.90 against December near 4.31 and March near 4.60, still support the dollar. Euro-dollar at 1.1052 is a fresh downside break. Dollar-yen at 160 is a five-year extreme, so the rate gap justifies a smaller long, not the full 20 million. Dollar-Canada and dollar-Swiss are already one-year extremes and are not new trades.
dollar-king.invalidation: The smaller dollar-yen long is wrong if the pair falls back through 158 or Japan closes the policy gap. The euro short is wrong if the ten-year gives back Friday's backup from 5.15 and the other dollar pairs stabilize together.

actions.note: Cut 12 million of the dollar-yen long, leaving 8 million. The rate gap still supports a smaller long at 160.

spot_candidate.rationale: Dollar-yen at 160 still has the rate gap, and 20 million is too much at a five-year extreme.

expression_memo.rationale: Dollar-yen is the policy-gap dollar. At 160 the expression stays, and the size comes down.

actions.note: Hold the 10 million euro-dollar short. The 1.1052 close is still a downside break.

spot_candidate.rationale: Euro-dollar at 1.1052 is a one-year percentile-zero downside break.

expression_memo.rationale: Euro-dollar remains the broad-dollar leg. No new pair clears a from-flat test at these extremes.

cross-merchant.thesis: The book stays flat. Australia-kiwi at 1.2266 is the same neighborhood as the short that was closed on 13 November, and a flat book would not sell it again while Brent at 95.84 still bids Australia. Australian dollar-Canada at 0.9675 is not rich, and buying it would reverse a closed fade while oil still supports Canada. Euro-sterling at 0.8356 and euro-yen at 176.83 are one-year location extremes without a policy gap in this tape. Dollar pairs are outside this remit.
cross-merchant.invalidation: Flat is wrong if Australia-kiwi is offered at a fresh extreme with an Australia-New Zealand policy gap actually in the tape, or if oil stops supporting Canada and Australian dollar-Canada develops a gap that is not a reverse of the closed fade.

actions.note: No non-dollar cross isolates a fresh gap that a flat book would initiate today.

expression_memo.rationale: Australia-kiwi is the closed winner, Australian dollar-Canada is an unchanged oil tape, and euro crosses have no policy wedge in this evidence.

postmortems.thesis_assessment: The richness fade was confirmed by the decline from about 1.2456 to about 1.2275, and closing it was the right process because that level was no longer a short to initiate.
postmortems.what_worked: The short used Australia-kiwi rather than the kiwi-dollar pair and was closed once a flat book would not re-initiate it.
postmortems.what_failed: The swing framing overstated how much downside remained after the cross had already left the entry extreme.
postmortems.no_new_lesson: The gain from the entry extreme to the 13 November close is bounded variance inside the risk budget, and the original process remains sound: cover the richness short when a flat book would not re-initiate it.

causal.original_belief: Australian dollar versus the kiwi near 1.2456 was a multi-year richness extreme, so the cross was the clean Australia-versus-New Zealand fade.
causal.observed_reality: The short was closed on 13 November after the cross had fallen to about 1.2275. The same cross now sits at 1.2266, with Brent still at 95.84.
causal.assumptions_right: The cross was the cleaner expression, the richness did fade, and covering once a flat book would not re-initiate it matched the evidence.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: The multi-week swing framing overstated residual downside once the cross had left the entry extreme, and New Zealand's policy path was never available.
causal.causal_divergence: The sign of the fade matched the belief. A few figures of leftover decline do not restore a short a flat book refused near 1.2275.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: With the same entry extreme the short would still be opened, and with the same 13 November tape the residual would still be closed rather than reloaded.
causal.future_implication: Do not reopen the Australia-kiwi short at 1.2266 while oil still bids Australia and no Australia-New Zealand policy gap is in the tape.

carry-is-king.thesis: Hold the 25 million March 2027 Canada bill receive. Cash near 2.30 against March near 3.03 is still a large premium over unchanged policy, and softer oil at Brent 95.84 and WTI 88.56 eases the energy threat that would force the Bank to deliver those hikes. The position is short that priced path by design. The path has not become more likely than the carry, and the missing Canada inflation print is not a reason to cut a markable receive.
carry-is-king.invalidation: Exit if Canada cash rises from about 2.30 toward the March implied rate near 3.03, or if oil-driven inflation makes the Bank deliver the priced hikes.

actions.note: Hold the March Canada receive. The premium over cash is intact.

rates_candidate.rationale: Cash near 2.30 versus March near 3.03 is still a large premium over unchanged Canadian policy.

spot_candidate.rationale: Long dollar-Canada earns the rate gap only by taking currency and oil beta.

expression_memo.rationale: The bill isolates the premium. Long dollar-Canada would add oil and currency risk instead of receiving it.

rate-hawk.thesis: Hold the US and Canada pays and close the Australia September pay. September 2027 SOFR near 4.82 and December 2026 near 4.31 are still hikes above 3.90 percent cash, and March 2027 Canada near 3.03 is still a hike above cash near 2.30. The two-year at 4.88 already sits above the front US futures. Australia September near 4.87 is not a hiking cycle against cash near 4.85, with March near 5.00 and the back priced for cuts. A hawkish seat is not a reason to keep the easy side of that strip. Euro September near 3.14 already matches the three-hike story, so no new euro pay is opened.
rate-hawk.invalidation: The US holds fail if December SOFR prices less than one hike above cash and the longer contracts give back the September jump. The Canada hold fails if March falls back toward 2.30 cash. The Australia close would be wrong only if September later repriced as a hike through the March contract.

actions.note: Hold 12.5 million September 2027 SOFR. The contract near 4.82 is still a hike above 3.90 cash.

rates_candidate.rationale: September SOFR near 4.82 is still a hike above 3.90 percent cash and still under the 4.88 percent two-year.

spot_candidate.rationale: Euro-dollar at 1.1052 is the spot twin of the US hike path, and it is already extended.

expression_memo.rationale: The hike path is in the September SOFR pay. Spot does not isolate the terminal rate.

actions.note: Hold 12.5 million March 2027 Canada. The contract near 3.03 is still a hike above cash near 2.30.

rates_candidate.rationale: March Canada near 3.03 against cash near 2.30 is still a hike path.

spot_candidate.rationale: Dollar-Canada at 1.4258 mixes the oil move with the policy path.

expression_memo.rationale: The Canada hike is still in the March bill. Dollar-Canada mixes oil into the policy path.

actions.note: Hold 10 million December 2026 SOFR. The contract near 4.31 is still a hike above 3.90 cash.

rates_candidate.rationale: December SOFR near 4.31 against cash at 3.90 is the front hike, and the two-year is already 4.88.

spot_candidate.rationale: Euro-dollar at 1.1052 is the spot twin of the US hike path, and it is already extended.

expression_memo.rationale: The unfinished piece is the front SOFR future under the two-year. That is a rates hold, not a new spot trade.

actions.note: Close the 20 million September 2027 Australia pay. The strip prices a flat front and cuts in the back, not a hiking cycle.

expression_memo.rationale: The Australian September pay is the easy side of a strip that prices cuts in the back. Closing it is the decision. No replacement is opened.

postmortems.what_failed: The June 2027 Australia pay failed as an underpriced hiking cycle. The strip stepped down instead of extending.
postmortems.thesis_assessment: A contract already above the then cash rate was treated as a hike that still had to be priced. The later strip was flat to lower.
postmortems.lesson: An Australian bill pay is not an underpriced hiking cycle once the strip is flat at the front and lower in the back.
postmortems.future_rule: Keep an Australian bill pay only while that contract is on a hike path above cash. A strip that is flat in front and lower in the back is an exit.

causal.original_belief: June 2027 Australia bills were only a modest step above cash, so an underpriced hiking cycle would lift the contract.
causal.observed_reality: The pay was closed on 13 November after the Australian strip stepped down and the contract was marked lower.
causal.assumptions_right: The bill, not the currency, was the right place to test the Australia path, and leaving once the strip stepped down kept the miss small.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: A contract already above cash was treated as a hike still to come. The chance that the strip would step down from the front was underweighted.

postmortems.no_new_lesson: The small loss one day after entry is bounded variance inside the risk budget. The original process remains sound because the pay was closed the next session once the strip still priced ease rather than a hike.

causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: Opening a contract already below cash treated a hawkish bias as a reason to pay a cut the strip was still pricing.
causal.causal_divergence: The intended mark was a rise toward the cash anchor. One session later the contract had not risen and the position was closed.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: With the same strip the December pay would not have been opened. If it had been opened, the next-day cover would still have been the action.

postmortems.what_failed: The March 2027 Canada pay was opened as a fade of a receive that looked rich to cash. The implied yield then fell, reductions locked in the loss, and the residual was covered only after that pay sat with the public hike story.
postmortems.thesis_assessment: The ownership objection was right at entry. The pay stopped being that fade once it became the hike consensus.
postmortems.lesson: A front-end pay is not an unowned fade just because the contract looks rich to cash. Once that pay is the public hike story, it is the crowded side.
postmortems.future_rule: Skip a new front-end pay or receive when the only crowding evidence is the gap to cash, unless a listed instrument shows the other side is the owned position and the working flow has stalled.

causal.original_belief: Paying March 2027 Canada bills would fade a receive that was already the owned front-end idea, and the gap versus cash was treated as proof that receive was crowded.
causal.observed_reality: The implied yield fell from the entry, reductions locked in the loss, and the residual was covered once that pay sat with the public hike story.
causal.assumptions_right: Another receive would have joined the crowd that was already owned. Cutting once the pay itself was the hike story matched the ownership rule.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: The cash gap was treated as if it proved the receive was wrong, while that receive kept being the winning flow. The short was then held into the window when the pay had become the crowded hike.
causal.causal_divergence: The crowded receive did not exhaust. It compressed, the fade lost money, and by the cover the position was the same hike expression the tape was already discussing.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: With the same entry information the pay should have been skipped. A cash gap plus an existing receive is not an ownership extreme.
causal.future_implication: Do not pay the next front contract because it looks rich to cash, and do not receive SOFR now only because headlines call the hike crowded while bond futures are still falling.

postmortems.what_worked: Shorting the extended Australia-kiwi cross and covering once that move was the visible trade captured the ownership asymmetry without joining a new crowded short.
postmortems.thesis_assessment: The extreme-cross fade was the right ownership trade and was closed when the move had become the visible trade.
postmortems.no_new_lesson: The original process remains sound. The gain was the intended fade of an extended cross, realized inside the risk budget, and it does not change the rule that a cash-gap receive is not an entry.

causal.original_belief: Australia-kiwi near 1.25 was the crowded long-cross extreme, a cleaner ownership fade than dollar-yen near its highs.
causal.observed_reality: The cross fell from the entry area and was covered once the move was already the visible trade.
causal.assumptions_right: The cross extreme was the owned side, the short paid, and covering once the move was visible avoided turning a completed fade into the new consensus short.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: A separate Canada pay was still on beside the cross. The cross fade did not need its full planned horizon once the move was the visible trade.
causal.causal_divergence: There was no material divergence. The extreme was faded, the cross mean-reverted, and the cover happened because the trade had become visible.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: With the same entry information the cross short was the right expression versus adding dollar-yen or another Canada receive.
causal.future_implication: Keep fading a cross only while it is the less-owned extreme, and cover it once the move is the visible trade.
